page: Amazon Web Services m8id.12xlarge is a general-purpose, instance-store equipped virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor delivering up to 3.9 GHz clock speeds across 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes an extensive 480 MB L3 cache and supports modern vector and matrix instructions, including AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity sits at 192.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Integrated local storage is a primary architectural differentiator for the m8id family, providing 2850 GB of direct NVMe SSD capacity. Network performance is provisioned with a 22 Gbps baseline bandwidth. In empirical benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-tier single-core performance alongside strong multi-core and memory throughput, clocking 195.99 GB/sec in large-block memory read bandwidth. Instruction set extensions and memory speeds contribute to high throughput in decompression tasks, static web serving (81.77 GB/sec), and in-memory cache processing, where Redis operations achieved 86.64 million operations per second.

From an efficiency standpoint, the m8id.12xlarge couples high-frequency DDR5 memory, massive L3 cache, and dedicated low-latency local NVMe storage into a single resource envelope. This architecture reduces dependence on detached block storage for ephemeral workloads and scratch disks. With its balance of CPU power, hardware matrix acceleration, and fast local I/O, the instance is well suited for large relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory caches, software compilation, CI/CD runners, batch data transformations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, it includes 192.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, a 22 Gbps baseline network interface, and 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions, delivering strong results in multi-core compute, data compression, and in-memory key-value processing reaching 86.64 million Redis operations per second. The combined density of fast DDR5 memory, substantial cache, and integrated high-speed local disk creates an efficient environment for I/O-sensitive applications without requiring remote storage attachments. This configuration is aligned with demanding workloads including high-concurrency relational databases, search indexing, distributed caching, enterprise continuous integration, and CPU-bound LLM prompt processing.
